# Pencil case

I keep a pencil in my bag. Some days it is the only tool I need.

The case also holds a thumbtack, a ruler, and some string. None of it matters much.

Writing is mostly deciding what to leave out. The rest takes care of itself, most days.

## Notes 1

The morning train is where most of the first drafts happen. Nobody asks for anything there.

A notebook with a soft cover bends to the shape of the bag and never complains about it.

Some sentences arrive whole. Most of them need three tries and a walk around the block.

Cutting a paragraph feels like losing something until the page reads better without it.

The best tool is the one that is already in your hand when the idea shows up.

Short words carry more weight than long ones, and they are easier to spell on a train.

Every draft has one line that only exists to get to the next one. That line can go.

Reading the page out loud finds the clumsy parts faster than reading it twice in silence.
